question: Train A leaves station M at 8:25 AM and reaches station N at 3:25 PM on the same day. Train B leaves station N at 10:25 AM and reaches station M at 3:25 PM on the same day. Find the time when trains A and B meet.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by Train A = 7 hours, and by Train B = 5 hours.

Let Total Distance = LCM of 7 and 5 = 35 units.

Speed of Train A = 5 units/hr, Speed of Train B = 7 units/hr.

Distance covered by Train A in 2 hours (8:25 AM to 10:25 AM) = 2 × 5 = 10 units.

Remaining distance = 25 units. Relative speed = 5 + 7 = 12 units/hr.

Time to meet = 25 ÷ 12 = 2 hours 5 minutes. Meeting Time = 10:25 AM + 2 hours 5 minutes = 12:30 PM.

**∴ The correct answer is 12:30 PM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Train A start time = 8:25 AM, arrival time = 3:25 PM

Train B start time = 10:25 AM, arrival time = 3:25 PM

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S₁ + S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total journey time for Train A = 3:25 PM − 8:25 AM = 7 hours

⇒ Total journey time for Train B = 3:25 PM − 10:25 AM = 5 hours

⇒ Let the total distance between M and N be the LCM of 7 and 5 = 35 km

⇒ Speed of Train A = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 km/h

⇒ Speed of Train B = 35 ÷ 5 = 7 km/h

⇒ Train A starts 2 hours earlier than Train B (from 8:25 AM to 10:25 AM).

⇒ Distance covered by Train A in these 2 hours = 5 × 2 = 10 km

⇒ Remaining distance to be covered together = 35 − 10 = 25 km

⇒ Relative speed of both trains = 5 + 7 = 12 km/h

⇒ Time taken to meet after 10:25 AM = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 25 ÷ 12 hours

⇒ 25 ÷ 12 hours = 2 hours and (1/12) × 60 minutes = 2 hours 5 minutes

⇒ Meeting time = 10:25 AM + 2 hours 5 minutes = 12:30 PM

**∴ The correct answer is 12:30 PM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = S₁ − S₂.

Average Speed

If an object covers equal distances at different speeds S₁ and S₂, the overall average speed is calculated as (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
